I worked in media for several years long before the industry and the rest of the country experienced significant turmoil. We were NEVER allowed to source people anonymously, because libel laws are strict if you’re wrong and someone decides to pursue legal action. Especially someone in a position of power. The best way to source something is to hear it for yourself. If you didn’t and it’s something sensational or as outrageous as a controversial comment, then make sure you source it from the most reliable sources. Political aides are not the most reliable sources. You may think media is agenda-driven (and many are), but political aides and staffers are among the least trustworthy. They’re young, incredibly ambitious to advance politically, and their lives are dedicated to their elected officials. They will do or say anything for you to publish what they want. Exaggerating and twisting facts are part of this. I never trusted a staffer with publishable details until I heard it from their superior.

A daily publication that prided itself on not wanting to publish anonymous sources. And no, they are not a “key facet of investigative journalism.” If you have sources that won’t go on the record, that’s fine. But then you make them point you to documents, emails, pictures, anything that will prove what they are saying. If your only way of proving something is an anonymous source with no evidence to back up what they’re saying, then you simply don’t have a source.

I wrote some pretty major stories at one point in my career. But the information that I sourced and printed only scratched the surface of what I was told had happened. The problem was I couldn’t PROVE most of the information I was being told because there were no witnesses, no documents, no emails. Nothing. It was all hearsay and rumor. The stories still ended up being huge in our community and state, but would have been devastating to many people had 100% of what I was being told proven true. And yes, I will admit I wish it was all true because of how significant it would have been. I concluded at the end that some of it probably happened but most of it was indeed rumor and hearsay. And I wasn’t going to risk my career to print rumor and hearsay in a story that was already very big. I wanted it to be completely sourced and accurate.

The problem is the media today are in such a rush to make certain public figures look foolish, they will run with anything from any source without taking the literal minutes it would take to fact check and source it. I worked with people who were like that and the sad thing is some of them moved up fast because they made waves with the public. I hate to say this, but media is a failing industry with much less talent than it has ever had in human history. And sadly our society is what pays the price in the end.
